caption: Psalm 22 recalls an ordinary birth and lifelong dependence on God. It never predicts that a Saviour will be born, and Luke makes no connection to it.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict the Saviour’s birth? The psalmist recalls being born and cared for from infancy. Luke reports that Mary gave birth to Jesus.
slides.body: The psalmist recalls being born and cared for from infancy. Luke reports that Mary gave birth to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict the Saviour’s birth?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:9-10: You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother's breast.
slides.body: You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother's breast.
slides.heading: Ps 22:9-10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 2:7, BSB: And she gave birth to her firstborn, a Son. She wrapped Him in swaddling cloths and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
slides.body: And she gave birth to her firstborn, a Son. She wrapped Him in swaddling cloths and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 2:7

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: A whole-life reading is possible Christians apply Psalm 22 to Jesus and Luke calls him Saviour elsewhere in the birth story.
slides.body: Christians apply Psalm 22 to Jesus and Luke calls him Saviour elsewhere in the birth story.
slides.heading: A whole-life reading is possible
